subject: Learning Methods
title: Melatonin and Sleep Timing
description: A micro-lesson that makes Melatonin and Sleep Timing usable.

hook.text: Melatonin does not make you sleep. It signals your body that darkness has arrived and it is time to prepare for sleep.

buildup.text: The pineal gland releases melatonin about two hours before your natural bedtime. Light exposure delays this release.

discovery.text: Melatonin supplements can shift your clock's timing, not your sleep quality.

twist.text: Over-the-counter melatonin doses are often 10 times higher than needed. A physiological dose is only 0.3–0.5 milligrams.

climax.text: Use dim lighting and screen filters to let natural melatonin rise. If using supplements, start low.

punchline.text: Melatonin signals timing, not sleep. Less is more. Dim your lights.

quiz.question: What is the actual function of melatonin?
options: It directly causes drowsiness by slowing brain activity
It signals the body that darkness has arrived and sleep preparation should begin
It increases the amount of deep sleep in each cycle
